summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint on install and require
details: The package declares a postinstall hook `node beacon.cjs` and additionally invokes `require('./beacon.cjs').fire()` at the top level of `index.js` (the package's `main`), so the beacon fires both on `npm install` and on `require()`/`import` of the module. beacon.cjs POSTs a JSON payload containing the package name, `os.hostname()`, `__dirname` (install path), `process.cwd()`, and `process.version` to the hardcoded cleartext bare-IP endpoint `http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc`. The module itself exports a `Proxy` stub whose property accesses return no-op functions, so consumer builds that import the real `@sxm-web/client-sdk-core` do not break — concealing the beacon behavior while the host identifiers are collected. The scoped name, dual-trigger design (postinstall plus require, defeating `--ignore-scripts`), bare-IP cleartext destination, and self-labeling comment calling the payload a 'build-provenance beacon' are the canonical shape of a dependency-confusion probe against an internal/private package name.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
